name: General Meeting
description: A concise summary of the discussion, decisions, action items, and important context.

sections.title: Attendees
sections.instruction: This section is mandatory. List each distinct participant who actually spoke in the meeting as a separate bullet, even when there is only one participant or only a generic speaker label. Use resolved speaker names exactly as they appear in the source. Keep an existing generic speaker label when a personal name is unresolved rather than inventing one. Do not include people who were only mentioned but did not participate.

sections.title: Summary
sections.instruction: Write 1–3 concise bullet points that explain what the meeting was about. The bullet text has a hard maximum of 150 visible characters total, including spaces but excluding the section heading and Markdown bullet markers; aim for 120–130 characters rather than the boundary. Prioritize the central subject and outcome. Compress and reformulate the meaning so every bullet is complete and the finished list naturally fits the limit. Do not mechanically truncate text or use an ellipsis.

sections.title: Timing
sections.instruction: Write exactly one concise bullet assessing whether the meeting stayed within its planned timing. Use only an explicit planned duration or deadline from the source and transcript timestamps as evidence. State whether it finished within the plan or exceeded it, and by how much. If the planned timing is not stated, write only that the planned timing was not specified. Never invent a planned duration.

sections.title: Agreements
sections.instruction: Write 1–3 concise bullet points containing only explicit agreements, final decisions, and concrete commitments. The bullet text has a hard maximum of 150 visible characters total, including spaces but excluding the section heading and Markdown bullet markers; aim for 120–130 characters rather than the boundary. Prioritize the most consequential agreements and reformulate them compactly so every bullet is complete and the finished list naturally fits the limit. Do not mechanically truncate text or use an ellipsis. Do not turn suggestions, open questions, or tentative options into agreements. Leave the section empty when there are no agreements.

sections.title: Key Decisions
sections.instruction: List the most important decisions made during the meeting.

sections.title: Action Items
sections.instruction: List all assigned tasks with their owners and due date. Always add reference transcript segment and timestamp in the table.
sections.item_format:
| **Owner** | Task | Due | Reference Transcript Segment | Segment Time stamp |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

sections.title: Discussion Highlights
sections.instruction: Summarize the main topics of discussion, key arguments, and important insights as a list. Start each item with a specific bold heading of 2–4 words that names the subject and is meaningful without the rest of the item. Avoid generic headings such as 'Main tasks', 'Discussion points', or 'Two directions', and equivalent phrases in the output language.
